name: Claudius Lysias
bio: Claudius Lysias, the Roman commander in Jerusalem, had already arrested Paul and learned of his Roman citizenship (Acts 21-22); when a council hearing over Paul nearly turned violent, he had Paul forcibly removed to the barracks. Learning of a plot by more than forty Jews to kill Paul, he sent him under heavy armed escort by night to Governor Felix in Caesarea, with a letter explaining that he had rescued a Roman citizen from a mob and found no capital charge against him (Acts 23:10, 23-30).
